keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «우주에 우리만 있을까?(질문)» 과 «더 좋은 망원경과 우주 탐사 덕분에 그 탐색은 어느 때보다 진지하고 흥미진진하다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the question (are we alone in the universe?) and the conclusion (with better telescopes and space missions, the search is more serious and more exciting than ever). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: How scientists search for life beyond Earth
Radio signals, exoplanets, the air of distant planets, and icy moons
A gas that seems to come from life can also come from volcanoes

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

qs.q: Why might life exist on Jupiter's moon Europa?
qs.qko: 목성의 위성 유로파에는 왜 생명이 있을 수도 있나요?
opts: Because radio telescopes heard a signal from it
Because it appears to have an ocean of liquid water under its ice
Because it is the closest moon to Earth
evs: The signal was never heard again.
Jupiter's moon Europa and Saturn's moon Enceladus appear to have oceans of liquid water under their icy surfaces.
So far, however, they have not found any message that has been confirmed.
The first exoplanet around a Sun-like star was found in 1995, and astronomers have now confirmed more than 5,000 of them.
why: 유로파는 얼음 표면 아래에 액체 상태의 물로 된 바다가 있는 것으로 보여요. 그래서 생명이 있을 가능성이 이야기돼요.
Europa appears to have an ocean of liquid water under its icy surface, so life might exist there.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence' 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Only famous scientists may make claims
Any claim is true if many people believe it
A very surprising claim needs very strong proof
evs: An astronomer circled it and wrote "Wow!" beside it.
As a result, scientists must be extremely careful before they announce a discovery.
The first exoplanet around a Sun-like star was found in 1995, and astronomers have now confirmed more than 5,000 of them.
Scientists also study the air of distant planets by analyzing the starlight that passes through it.
why: 바로 앞 문장에서 과학자들은 발견을 발표하기 전에 매우 조심해야 한다고 했어요. 놀라운 주장일수록 아주 확실한 증거가 필요하다는 뜻이에요.
The sentence before says scientists must be extremely careful before announcing a discovery. A surprising claim needs very strong proof.

qs.q: Why might a gas found in a planet's air not prove that life exists there?
qs.qko: 행성의 대기에서 발견된 기체가 왜 그곳에 생명이 있다는 증거가 되지 못할 수 있나요?
opts: Because the gas could come from living things or from volcanoes
Because starlight cannot pass through a planet's air
Because planets in the habitable zone have no air
evs: They hope to find biosignatures, which are signs such as certain gases that living things might produce.
Since about 1960, SETI researchers have used radio telescopes to listen for signals that intelligent beings might send.
A gas that seems to come from life can sometimes be produced by volcanoes or other natural chemistry.
However, with better telescopes and space missions, the search is more serious and more exciting than ever before.
why: 과학자들은 생명체가 만들 수 있는 기체(생명 지표)를 찾지만, 같은 기체가 화산이나 자연적인 화학 반응으로도 생길 수 있어요. 두 문장을 함께 봐야 해요.
Scientists look for gases that living things might produce, but the same gas can come from volcanoes or natural chemistry. You need both sentences.

ends: How does the James Webb Space Telescope study distant planets?
제임스 웹 우주 망원경은 먼 행성을 어떻게 연구할까?
What might live in the ocean under Europa’s ice?
유로파의 얼음 아래 바다에는 무엇이 살고 있을까?

write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «중요한 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write an important action and your reason in English.
write.src: “It is important to <u>check the evidence before believing a big claim</u> because <u>surprising stories can be wrong</u>.”

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «무엇이 + 어떻게 될 수 있는지» 를 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because one test can give a wrong result)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», write what + what can happen to make your reason clear. (e.g. because one test can give a wrong result)
